about: Every Jev question set the Flock puts to `POST /v1/systemone` during a run. `flock_step`, read by factory/flock/step_reading.mjs once per green story step; and `flock_peer_rewrite`, read by factory/flock/engine.mjs when an edit replaces a peer's lines; their modes live in factory/policy.json's `flock.jev_step` and `flock.jev_peer_rewrite`. The authoring sets live beside their readers, in skills/ultrawrite/stories/questions.json (#1449). Each set names its reader and its rollback (map #1131 rule 3). A question is literal: it names no policy word, and nothing here decides anything. A Jev `null` routes that reading to the set's stated rollback, never to a guess. A reworded question is a different question: its readings mean something else.

flock_step.when: At a ready settle, once per story, at its last green step (#1369)
flock_step.provenance: state-probe runner spec 2026-09-27 §7; TypeSafe citation-check recipe (supports / contradicts / says nothing)

instructions.question: After the user did `did`, do `after` and `screen_text` show that `story` came true?
instructions.context: `story` is the sentence the operator signed. `before` and `after` are the app's store as [tables, values] before the story's first step and after its last; row ids are numbered by creation order. When the store is too big to send whole, `changes` stands in for `before` and `after`: one {table, row, before, after} per row that differs, a missing row null. `screen_text` is the page's visible text after the last step. `did` is everything the user clicked or typed, every step of the story in order.

criteria.supports: The store or the screen after the step shows the outcome the sentence describes
criteria.contradicts: The store or the screen shows something the sentence rules out
criteria.says_nothing: The evidence neither shows nor rules out the sentence's outcome

flock_peer_rewrite.when: When an agent's edit replaces or deletes lines a peer wrote, once per such edit (#1401)
flock_peer_rewrite.rollback: factory/policy.json flock.jev_peer_rewrite.mode = record (never drafts), or off (never asks)
flock_peer_rewrite.provenance: weave census 2026-09-29 (#1401): run-277's only edit over a peer's line ran two of the peer's words together; operator pick 2026-09-29

instructions.question: Does `after` still carry the change the peer made when it turned `before` into `peer`?
instructions.context: `path` is the file. `before` is what the peer's lines replaced (empty when the peer only added them), and `peer` is what the peer wrote. `after` is what a second agent then wrote over the peer's lines (empty when it deleted them). `tasks` are the two sides, the second agent's first, each with its `title` and its `claim`, what that side meant.

criteria.keeps: What the peer changed is still there in `after`, beside the second agent's own change
criteria.loses: Part of the peer's change is undone, or `after` runs together words or lines that `before` and `peer` kept apart
criteria.supersedes: The second agent's claim means to replace the peer's change, and `after` does exactly that
